label: input k in a sequence starting with x and rich in s/z/n/w
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.003% of steps) that fires almost only when the input token is k (99% of mass), during the original phase, mostly at positions 4-6. It is strongly gated by the prefix: the first original token is x (86% of mass), and the strongest activations come when the earlier tokens are mostly from {s, z, n, w, x} (e.g. x z z s e r k, x z s z k). Prefixes holding other letters, vowels or digits give weak or no activation. It does not fire on k in the copy phase, on k at positions 0-2, or on any token other than k. Input k with first token x alone gives high recall (78%, 85% of mass) but precision of only 5%. Also requiring at least 3 tokens from {x,s,z,n,w} before the k raises dev F1 to 0.50 (precision 0.48, recall 0.53, mass recall 0.70). The remaining dependence on the prefix seems graded, like a direction in the hidden state, rather than a clean boolean rule. Some activations occur without a leading x when s/z/n/w are present.
